This hearing has been done through hybrid mode.
2. The Petitioner is the Khanpur Market Association Regd. (hereinafter 'the Association') which has 34 shopkeepers as its members.

The Petitioner has filed the present petition challenging the impugned notice issued by the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board (DUSIB) by which the shopkeepers are being directed to remove their belongings and themselves from the shops in view of the construction of the Aerocity-Tughlakabad corridor of the MRTS project phase-IV.

The said notice reads as under:
"It is informed that on Khanpur M. B. Road, DMRC carrying on construction of Aerocity-Tughlakabad corridor of MRTS Project Ph-IV, due to which the Khanpur Khanpur Market Association Regd vs Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board ... on 14 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168493845/

sentences.text: These shops are encroached on the government land of DUSIB, which is required for the completion of DMRC project.

It is requested that in the next 7 (seven) days, the earmarked shops should remove all their belongings and by themselves remove the shops otherwise legal/lawful action will be taken and DUSIB will not be responsible for any damage caused due the action taken."

3. As per the writ petition, the Association consists of members who are shopkeepers and squatters running small and petty businesses from the shops/juggis situated in Mehrauli Badarpur (M.B.)
Road, Khanpur Market, New Delhi- 110062.
According to the Petitioners, they have been running their businesses for the last 50 years in this particular location and belong to the vulnerable communities.
In support of the writ petition, they have filed some documents to show that they are in actual uninterrupted possession.
4. The details of the shopkeepers is mentioned in annexure P-3 with other contact details and identity details of the Petitioner members.

5. The case of the Petitioners is that the Petitioners are being dispossessed without fair compensation as required under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, ('Fair Compensation Act') and that they are not being compensated even though they are 'Project Affected Families' and 'Project Affected Persons'.
6.

In the meantime, till the next date of hearing the respondents are directed to maintain the status quo with regard to the shops in possession of the members of the petitioner association.
The Respondents who are DUSIB, DMRC and the DM (South) have contested the present writ petition.
An application for vacation of stay has been filed by both DUSIB and DMRC along with their counter affidavits.

As per the applications filed by them, the Petitioners would not be covered by the statute relating to Land Acquisition i.e. the Fair Compensation Act as the land in question where the Petitioners are located is public land which the Petitioners have encroached.
The submission of the Respondents is that the Petitioners cannot be treated equally with other private owners in the Khanpur area, in order to claim rehabilitation and compensation.
It is submitted that the construction work on the entire corridor itself has come to a standstill because of the interim order which is operating in the present case.

Ld. Counsels for the Respondents submit that there was a deliberate intention to not serve not even one Nominated Counsel for the Respondents, only to ensure that the authorities are not represented before the Vacation Bench, before whom the matter was listed.

9. Mr. Chauhan, ld. Counsel appearing for the DUSIB submits that the Khanpur Harijan camp and Banjara camp which is notified in the notified JJ clusters does not include the shops, as, under the Delhi Slum & JJ Rehabilitation and Relocation Policy, 2015, commercial shops are not covered.

However, only the shops which are illegally encroaching the area next to the main road on the MB Road are being removed for construction of the Aerocity-Tughlakabad corridor of the MRTS project phase-IV.
11. This Court observes that the struggle between rehabilitation and redevelopment, is an ongoing one.
In the city of Delhi, various policies have been introduced for providing rehabilitation and shelters for jhuggi jhopri clusters.

Insofar as the RFC Act is concerned, clearly, the said Act would not be applicable to the present case as a reading of Section 2 of the RFC Act makes it clear that the same applies when Government acquires others' land for a public purpose.
It would obviously not apply to removal of encroachments from public or Government land.

15. In the present case, photographs which have been placed on record by the Petitioners as also the Respondents does not show any residential premises.
The area primarily encompasses shops which are selling various items including cane goods, some jute ware, hardware, pottery, plastic wired cots (manjis/charpoys) and other such items.
16. The Petitioners claim that there are some residences in the said area.

However, even after considering the documents filed along with the photographs as also the additional documents handed across in Court today, the Court is not convinced that there are any residential premises within or besides these shops.

Counsel for the Petitioners relies upon the communication dated 14th July, 1984 signed by the Director (Slums), Delhi Development Authority, addressed to Shri G. Swamy Nayak, Member of Parliament wherein it was assured that there was no proposal for removal of the Sirkiwalas from the said present site.
The said letter also stated that if however, the Sirkiwalas are removed they will be provided alternate sites according to the policy of alternative allotment.

The said communication reads as under:
"Kindly refer to your letter dated 9.5.1984 addressed to the Lt. Governor, Delhi,
regarding allotment of plots/construction or market for the Sirkiwalas.
Presently there is no proposal for the removal of these sirkiwalas trom their present site of working/marketing.

However, I have issued instructions to the Deputy Director (L&R) of the Slum Department that if any persons doing the business of Sirki are removed from the Slum/JJ colony from their existing site they should be provided alternative sites according to the policy of alternative allotment/eligibility"
18.

Insofar as the jhuggis and residences as also any families who may be residing there are concerned, some directions are being issued to safeguard their interest.

The said community centre shall be available to the members of the Petitioner Association and their family members for at least for a period of three months and in case the members of the Association, and their family requests for more time, they are free to approach this Court by way of an application.
ii. The members of the Petitioner Association, whoever wish to shift their belongings or their family members, if any, to the said community centre may do so within one week.

After a period of one week, the interim order passed by this Court on 2nd January, 2023 shall no longer be operative.
The DMRC and DUSIB are free to commence the work in respect of the Aerocity-Tughlakabad Corridor of the MRTS project.

vi. Considering the fact that Harijan camp and Banjara camp opposite PNB Khanpur is notified as a JJ cluster notified by DUSIB, under the rehabilitation policy, the DUSIB shall undertake a verification as to whether any of the members of the Petitioner Association are entitled to rehabilitation.
If any of the members are considered eligible for rehabilitation, then their cases shall be processed in accordance with law in an expeditious manner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Insofar as the RFC Act is concerned, clearly, the said Act would not be applicable to the present case as a reading of Section 2 of the RFC Act makes it clear that the same applies when Government acquires others' land for a public purpose.
It would obviously not apply to removal of encroachments from public or Government land.
Moreover, the Delhi Slum & JJ Rehabilitation and Relocation Policy, 2015 which provides mandatory rehabilitation for people living in the JJ clusters which are notified by DUSIB, is applicable to residential jhuggi jhopris and not commercial shops.
This is clear from a reading of the definition 2(f) of the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board Act, 2010.
The said definition reads as:
(f) "jhuggi" means a structure whether temporary or pucca, of whatever material made, with the following characteristics, namely:-
(i) it is built for residential purpose;
(ii) its location is not in conformity with the land use of the Delhi Master Plan;
(iii) it is not duly authorized by the local authority having jurisdiction; and (iv) it is included in a jhuggi jhopri basti declared as such by the Board, by notification;
13.
14. A conjoint reading of Section 2(f) of the DUSIB Act read with Definition 1(viii) and 1(ix) of the Delhi Slum & JJ Rehabilitation and Relocation Policy, 2015 makes it clear that the policy of providing rehabilitation would not be applicable to the commercial shops.
However, insofar as the families who may be living beside or above the commercial shops are concerned, some consideration could be given for the relocation and rehabilitation of such families.
15. In the present case, photographs which have been placed on record by the Petitioners as also the Respondents does not show any residential premises.
The area primarily encompasses shops which are selling various items including cane goods, some jute ware, hardware, pottery, plastic wired cots (manjis/charpoys) and other such items.
16. The Petitioners claim that there are some residences in the said area.
In view of the above facts, it is clear that the Petitioners who are traders running commercial shops would not be entitled to compensation under the RFC Act.
Insofar as the jhuggis and residences as also any families who may be residing there are concerned, some directions are being issued to safeguard their interest.
